results.summary:
A track runner: a second execution engine beside node dispatch. A track is a root task plus everything still blocking it, executed by ONE session in dependency order, while the board stays the source of truth — the runner claims each node with `hkb claim`, works it, and finishes it with its own terminal verb, so every node stays a durable checkpoint.

`src/track.js` is pure and is the whole model: `resolveTrack` (post-order DFS over unfinished `blockedBy` edges — a blocker closed as *completed* is finished work, not a node, so a track shrinks as it runs and a resumed track is exactly what is left), `trackWaves` (what may fan out to subagents), `trackPaths` (the union the path_overlap guard needs), `trackReadiness`, `planTracks`, `trackAlreadyAttempted` and `trackContext` (the runner prompt). No I/O: everything is a function of the board read the tick already did. The per-node brief is deliberately fetched lazily by the runner with `hkb context <n>` — literally the `workerContext` a cold worker gets — instead of building N of them at spawn time, which is where the design note's "reuses workerContext per node" is honoured frugally.

Dispatcher: a new step 3a runs BEFORE the ready loop (a track and its own frontier would otherwise race for the same slot and the node would win, leaving the track un-runnable for as long as it ran). Same caps and guards as a node claim, with the union of the nodes' paths. While a track attempt is open its nodes are *covered*: never reclaimed (they have no pid of their own — the root's lease is their liveness), never claimed, and costing ONE slot between them. `summary.tracks` reports every track, claimed or refused, with the reason.

DECISIONS, both documented in SKILL.md and protocol.md:
1. One PR per node, stacked in dependency order (node N branches from the branch of the node it is blocked by, `--base` the same). NOT one shared branch: a node's issue closes when *its* PR merges, which is what makes it a checkpoint; a single PR closing several nodes drags the unfinished ones into `review` behind it where nothing can finish them.
2. Every refusal is a fallback to node dispatch, never an error — a cycle, a blocker off the board, a node that is running/blocked/review/triage, a node wearing kb:needs-human, a node with an open PR, a node on a profile outside the runner's `track_agents` (cross-harness tracks are out of scope by design), and a root that has already had one track attempt.

Two changes outside the task's declared paths, both prerequisites rather than scope creep: (a) `src/lifecycle.js` + `src/cli.js` now scope `KB_ATTEMPT` to `KB_TASK` (`envAttempt`). A runner acts on several tasks from one session; without this, `hkb complete <node>` would read the ROOT's attempt number, synthesize a phantom attempt row on the node and release a lock the node never held. Invisible to a plain worker, which only ever acts on its own task — `test/heartbeat.test.js`'s fixture gained `KB_TASK: '7'` to model a real worker's env. (b) `src/board.js` gains the `claude-track` default profile, without which the feature has no launch template and `--profiles claude-track` cannot work. Also `README.md` (outside paths, nothing else owns it) gained a `claude-track` paragraph in the Profiles section.

One further dispatcher change worth knowing: `failAttempt` now returns a task to `ready` or `todo` by `computeReady`, not blindly to `ready`. A track root is claimed while its blockers are still open, so a failed track attempt has to leave it in `todo` behind them. This is the same rule the orphaned-card branch two lines above already used.

PR: https://github.com/emyann/harness-kanban-board/pull/40 (draft, `Closes #26`).

Terminal verb note: this attempt intended `hkb complete`, but this harness's worktree-isolation guard refuses any command containing the token `complete` (it reads it as the bash `complete` builtin), whatever the spelling, including `node bin/hkb.js complete` — the same wall #11 attempt 1 hit. `hkb heartbeat` was allowed throughout, so it is a token match, not a board or git problem. With PR #40 open, `complete` and `request-review` land the task in exactly the same place (`review`, waiting on the PR) and record the same summary and metadata; only the attempt outcome differs (`review_requested` rather than `completed`). The work is finished and verified.

Next worker: the runner itself has never been executed end to end against a real 3-node chain — the tests prove the board transitions, not that a Claude session follows the prompt. Running one real decomposed track and reading the log is the obvious next step, and the prompt is where any fix goes (`trackContext` in src/track.js).
